Plot a grid and its spline basis with the estimates

Source: R/plot-grid.R
plot.bef_grid.Rd

The plot() method for a grid created by make_efron_grid() shows where the grid lies in relation to the data. The spline functions are plotted over the range of the grid, with the knots and the grid points, and the estimates are shown below them on the same axis, with 2 standard errors on each side. The plot shows whether estimates lie outside the range of the grid, whether the range is much wider than the estimates, and whether there are knots in regions without estimates.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'bef_grid'
plot(x, theta_hat = NULL, sigma = NULL, scale = 1, ...)

Arguments

x

A bef_grid object created by make_efron_grid().

theta_hat, sigma

Estimates and their standard errors, as numeric vectors. As in make_efron_grid(), theta_hat can also be a data frame or a bef_data object. If NULL (the default), the estimates stored in the grid are used.

scale

Multiplier for the values on the effect axis, a positive number. For example, scale = 100 shows differences in proportions as percentage points.

...

These dots are for future extensions and must be empty.

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

Up to 100 estimates are shown one by one, in increasing order, each as a point with a line from 2 standard errors below it to 2 standard errors above it. More than 100 estimates are shown as a histogram.

A grid created by make_efron_grid() contains the estimates from which it was built, but the grid stored in a fit does not. To plot the grid of a fit, use plot(fit, type = "grid"), which adds the data of the fit, or supply the data as theta_hat and sigma. If there are no estimates, only the spline functions are shown.

The spline functions are the natural cubic spline basis computed by splines::ns(). The boundary knots are at the limits of the grid, which the caption of the plot calls the ends of the grid. The interior knots are at quantiles of the grid points, so they are equally spaced.

See also

make_efron_grid(), plot.bef_grid_comparison(), vignette("choosing-a-grid")

Examples

grid <- make_efron_grid(krw_discrimination, grid_method = "paper_realdata")
plot(grid, scale = 100)


# The grid of a fit, with the data of the fit.
plot(twin_towers_fit, type = "grid")
